name: Superior thalamic radiation
summary: The superior thalamic radiation carries the fibers between the ventral tier of the thalamus and the sensorimotor cortex through the capsule's posterior limb and the corona radiata: the ventral posterior nuclei's somatosensory projection to the postcentral gyrus and the ventrolateral and ventral anterior nuclei's motor projection to the precentral gyrus and premotor cortex. It is the thalamocortical half of the sensorimotor system, running beside the descending corticospinal fibers, so posterior limb lesions produce sensory and motor deficits together, and thalamocortical disconnection in the corona radiata produces cortical-type sensory loss with an intact thalamus.

anatomy.location: From the ventral anterior, ventrolateral and ventral posterior nuclei laterally through the capsule's posterior limb, interdigitating with the corticospinal tract, and upward through the corona radiata to the precentral and postcentral gyri and the paracentral lobule, with the leg fibers posterior and the face fibers anterior in the capsule.

afferents.from: Ventral posterior, ventrolateral and ventral anterior nuclei

efferents.to: Postcentral and precentral gyri, premotor cortex
Ventral thalamic nuclei and reticular nucleus

function: It delivers touch, proprioception, pain and temperature from the ventral posterior nuclei to the somatosensory cortex and the cerebellar and pallidal motor signals from the ventrolateral and ventral anterior nuclei to the motor and premotor cortex, and it returns corticothalamic fibers that regulate thalamic gating and generate sleep spindles and the alpha rhythm through the reticular nucleus. Its interruption produces contralateral hemianesthesia of cortical type (impaired localization, two-point discrimination and graphesthesia with relative preservation of pain) and contributes to ataxia and bradykinesia from loss of the motor thalamic input. It is damaged in lenticulostriate and anterior choroidal infarcts and in periventricular hemorrhage.

imaging.normalAppearance: On tractography a superoinferior bundle from the lateral thalamus through the posterior limb to the pre- and postcentral gyri, inseparable from the corticospinal tract on conventional images.

pathology.finding: Restricted diffusion of the posterior limb with contralateral hemiparesis and hemisensory loss.

pathology.finding: Small deep white-matter infarct interrupting thalamocortical fibers with impaired discriminative sensation and a normal thalamus.
